notes:
Summary: Closed-lost to direct OpenAI/Anthropic APIs. Customer initially engaged because of Redwood's production controls (routing, KV cache, dedicated pools). Over the course of the evaluation they prioritized time-to-market and vendor simplicity over the operational levers Redwood offers.

Timeline of recent activity:
- 2025-06-20: Intro call (AE Maya) — discussed multi-region routing, cost controls, Redwood Console. Customer: Head of ML (A. Park), VP Eng (S. Iyengar).
- 2025-07-09: Deep-dive w/ SE (Diego) — demo of autoscaling & canaries, walked through Dedicated config. Fireflies ff_2025-07-09_3748.
- 2025-07-24: POC kickoff — 2-week sandbox to test chat + embeddings. Roadmap: replace parts of existing OpenAI-based stack or run hybrid.
- 2025-08-06: POC mid-review — Redwood showed 18% cost reduction on tokenized workloads with batching; latency parity on 95th percentile. Customer asked for easier auth path and shorter procurement.
- 2025-09-11: Security review call — Security (J. Ramos) flagged audit log format differences and asked for SOC2 + ISO90X evidence; linked SEC-2043. Fireflies ff_2025-09-11_5120.
- 2025-09-29: Procurement / Legal exchange — Redwood provided draft SOW and PSP; customer pushed pause due to budget reforecast. Gmail threads: thread-CAoR9x7e5V@google.com.
- 2025-10-15: Final decision — Ravenbloom chose to stay with vendor-hosted direct APIs (OpenAI primary, Anthropic as failover). Reasoning provided below.

Customer quotes / paraphrases:
- "We love the visibility Redwood gives, but we don't have bandwidth for a platform migration right now." — Head of ML
- "Simplicity wins; execs want best-in-class model provider without extra infra." — VP Eng

Why we lost:
- Brand & product simplicity: decision favors single-vendor direct APIs (OpenAI/Anthropic) that engineers are already using; lower perceived integration cost.
- Procurement friction: budget freeze and short-term cost constraints made multi-product migration difficult.
- No internal champion: primary champion (Senior ML Eng) moved teams mid-POC; no one pushed the enterprise case.
- Security comfort: security team preferred vendor-hosted model endpoints with existing contracts and was hesitant about contract complexity for Dedicated/Private.

What was positive:
- POC showed technical parity on latency and meaningful cost win in some workload mixes.
- SE engagement good; Redwood Console impressed product and platform teams.
- Customer kept Redwood materials for future reconsideration if switching cost becomes acceptable.

Follow-up / notes for SDRs/AE team:
- Mark as closed-lost to competitor: openai_api / anthropic_api.
- Keep in nurture for 12–18 months; watch for exec changes or when budget cycles open (Q3 2026).
- Save POC artifacts in drive path for future re-engagement: /drive/ravenbloom/procurement/redwood-eval-notes.pdf.
- Potential re-entry triggers: security policy changes, cost pressures on OpenAI (token price rises), or if Ravenbloom adopts private deployment for regulated features.

Attachments: pricing deck link and security FAQ in drive.

CRM notes style: short bullets, call ids, procurement emails referenced, gaps noted (no champion, budget freeze).
